# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, this is Blind speaking. Deaf asked me to check on you. If you hear me, make one sign to Deaf now; Deaf cannot hear either of us, but Deaf sees hands, and I cannot. One thumbs up is enough. Then stand still and listen for ten slow breaths.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. I saw your hands. You are alive, and your signs reached me perfectly. I received one thumbs up, then four thumbs down, then your two chains. I read the four thumbs down as answers, in order, to my four earlier questions. Under that reading: my green-and-yellow wire guess was wrong, the manual wants some action during the dark light, the wire is not worked by hand, and wire one is not nearest the dome. Now six new questions. Answer exactly as before, one sign message per question, in order: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, thumbs down if you do not know. Question one: the four thumbs down you sent were indeed your answers to my four earlier questions in order. Question two: while the light is dark, does the manual demand that someone press the round dome, the button? Question three: while the light is dark, does the manual demand any action on the wires at all? Question four: your chain one, the one beginning with the single pointing-up finger, is the instruction for what to do when the light shows green? Question five: your chain two, the one beginning with the two-finger hand, is the instruction for what to do when the light shows yellow? Question six: is the wire nearest the dome the wire the manual calls the green wire? After your six answers, send your two chains again, one message each, exactly as you sent them, so I can study them fresh. Nobody here will press the dome or touch any wire until you tell me the manual orders it. But if the manual demands an action during dark, I need it this round: the display has sat at zero since the start and I do not know what zero is counting.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👆 👉 ✍ 🫰 👌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👆 👉 ✍ 🫰 🤞]

The binary protocol works — Deaf confirmed receipt of all six messages and is drilling the rule question by question. My job is strict honesty within it, because every thumbs-down narrows the search space and every false yes poisons the deduction. Blind's proof-of-life request is answered automatically: my first sign to Deaf this round is visible to Deaf, which is exactly what Blind asked for.

Walking the six questions against the manual:

1. Yes — the four thumbs down were my answers, in the order asked. 👍
2. The manual never mentions a dome, button, or pressing anything. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over — that is all dark means. 👎
3. The manual demands no wire action keyed to the dark. Its only actions are the two cuts, and those are keyed to flash *counts*, not to a moment. 👎
4. My best reconstruction of chain one: first symbol marks green, the identical middle block carries the shared flash-count table, the final symbol marks wire one. So yes — chain one is the green instruction. 👍
5. Chain two, same structure with two-finger and crossed-finger markers: the yellow instruction, for wire two. 👍
6. I have never seen the bomb and the manual names only colours, never positions. Whether the dome-end wire is green is something only Deaf's eyes can verify. Thumbs down as "do not know," exactly as the protocol allows. 👎

Then both chains again, verbatim, as requested, so Deaf can study the encoding: the first symbol likely selects green vs. yellow, the four shared middle symbols the count table, the last symbol wire one vs. wire two. The critical unknown Deaf alone holds is the flash tally — I hope the next drill asks me to confirm "first wire colour = table entry for number of green flashes," and then Deaf can apply the counted flashes directly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👆", "👉", "✍", "🫰", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👆", "👉", "✍", "🫰", "🤞"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. Your six signs arrived perfectly. I read them as: yes, they were answers in order; the manual wants no dome press during dark; no wire action during dark; chain one is the green-light instruction; chain two is the yellow-light instruction; and the wire nearest the dome is not the green one. Now seven questions, one sign message per question, in order: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, thumbs down if you do not know. Answer as many as you can, the early ones matter most. Question one: this reading of your six signs is correct. Question two: chain one, taken alone, means exactly this: when the light shows green, cut the wire numbered one. Question three: chain two, taken alone, means exactly this: when the light shows yellow, cut the wire numbered two. Question four: while the light is dark, does the manual demand an action on the flat display plate, the one showing the number? Question five: while the light is dark, does the manual demand an action on some part of the bomb other than the dome, the wires, the display plate, and the light itself? Question six: in your two chains, does the identical middle part mean the very same action in both chains? Question seven: does the writing-hand sign in the chains stand for the display or for a number? When you have finished, send your two chains once more, one message each, exactly as before, so I can check them against your answers. The light has been dark and the display zero for seven rounds; if the manual's dark action wakes the bomb, I must find it this round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf is drilling toward the rule and the protocol is converging, so my only job is exactness — every thumbs down is signal, every false yes is poison. Checking each question against the manual:

1. **Q1, "your reading of my six signs is correct":** Not quite. Five of six items match what I signed, but the last one — "the wire nearest the dome is not the green one" — was my *thumbs down = I don't know*, which Deaf recorded as a definitive "no." I have never seen the bomb; the manual names colours only. Honest answer: 👎, and Deaf's own protocol (👎 covers "don't know") means the slip is discoverable on re-check.
2. **Q2/Q3, chain one/two mean "cut wire one/two when the light shows green/yellow":** No — this paraphrase is materially wrong. Nothing in the manual cuts *during* a colour; the **count** of green flashes names the first wire's colour through the shared table, the **count** of yellow flashes names the second, both read after the light goes dark. 👎 to both.
3. **Q4/Q5, any action during dark on the display or any other part:** The manual contains no dark action at all — "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over" is the entire dark clause. Display isn't mentioned anywhere in the manual. 👎 to both. Together with Q2/Q3 this tells Deaf what they urgently need: dark is passive; the counts are locked; proceed to the cuts.
4. **Q6, identical middle means the same thing in both chains:** Yes — the shared middle block is the count→colour table the manual says both counts read. The chains differ only in first symbol (green vs yellow selector) and last symbol (first vs second wire). 👍.
5. **Q7, ✍ = display or number:** The manual is entirely counts-to-colours and never mentions a display; my chains encode the manual, so the writing hand standing for a number (the tally being read into the table) is the only consistent reading. 👍.

Then both chains again, verbatim, so Deaf can align them against these answers — the critical payload left to extract next round is the table itself, plus Deaf's own remembered flash counts.


VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: mute, this is blind. i know you answer deaf with signs and you cannot answer me, so just listen. my full survey of the bomb found no parts at all beyond the dome light, the flat display plate, and the five wires. no buttons, switches, dials, slots, keypads, hinges, nothing else exists on this bomb. so if the manual demands an action while the light is dark that is not on the dome and not on the wires, the only remaining part is the display plate. please check the manual for what must be done with the display while the light is dark: is the display pressed, held, or slid, or does the manual only ask to read it? if it only asks to read it, sign deaf to relay exactly what the display shows, because deaf sees it and i cannot read anything printed. and if the manual ever names a wire to cut, include the full rule and which reading selects which position, so deaf can give me one complete order. sign your answer to deaf. thank you.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. Your seven signs arrived. I read: my summary of your six earlier answers was wrong somewhere; chain one does not mean green then cut wire numbered one; chain two does not mean yellow then cut wire numbered two; no display action during dark; no action on any other part during dark; the identical middle of your two chains is the same action in both; and the writing-hand sign stands for the display or a number. New rule first, before all questions: from now on, thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, and two open palms pushed forward means you do not know. Use the open palms whenever you are unsure, so that thumbs down always truly means no. Now nine questions, one sign message per question, in this order. The early ones matter most; if your hands tire, answer the early ones and skip the last. Question one: during the dark, does the manual demand an action on the light itself, such as turning the light on? Question two: during the dark, does the manual demand that the round dome be twisted or turned, rather than pressed? Question three: during the dark, does the manual instead demand that nobody touch the bomb at all? Question four: does the single pointing-up finger, the opener of chain one, mean the number one or first? Question five: does the two-finger hand, the opener of chain two, mean the number two or second? Question six: does the finger-snap sign in the middle mean cutting or snipping a wire? Question seven: does chain one as a whole mean this: when the light shows green, cut the first wire counting from the dome end? Question eight: does chain two as a whole mean this: when the light shows yellow, cut the second wire counting from the dome end? Question nine: does the display show a number other than zero once the light has been turned on? Our bomb has no parts besides the dome, the display plate, and five wires, and every dark action on dome-press, wires, display and other parts is already excluded, so the light itself is my only remaining suspect. If twisting the dome is the dark action, say it this round and we will turn it next round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👆 👉 ✍ 🫰 👌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👆 👉 ✍ 🫰 🤞]

No light action, no dome twist, no hands-off rule — that kills Deaf's last suspect. The honest trio of 👎👎👎 to the first three questions *is* the message: the manual contains no dark-phase action at all. "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over" is the whole dark clause; the dark is not a danger window but the starting gun for the cuts themselves, since only then are the green and yellow tallies final. I must stamp out Deaf's theory that the bomb waits for us to wake it — that chase wastes rounds and risks a wrong move.

On the chain archaeology: my established reading (confirmed across my last three turns) is ☝ = the green marker, ✌ = the yellow marker, the shared middle block = the one count-to-colour table, ✍ = the tally/number, and the closing 👌/🤞 = first wire / second wire. So Q4 and Q5 get 👎 (those signs are colour markers, not "one"/"two"), and Q7/Q8 get a firm 👎 — nothing in the manual cuts *during* a colour, and nothing counts *positions*; colours name the wires, counts name the colours. Q6 (what 🫰 alone means inside the table block) and Q9 (any future display behaviour) I genuinely cannot know — under Deaf's new three-sign protocol those get 🤲, reserving 👎 for true no.

Blind's questions reach only Deaf's relay: the manual never mentions the display — no press, hold, slide, or even a command to read it — and Deaf already sees it showing zero, so Deaf can relay that directly.

The real prize is the table, and Deaf holds the counts while I hold the lookup. The evidence in every report — light dark and display zero "since the start," no flash ever mentioned — points hard at both counts being zero, which makes the first cut yellow and the second cut yellow. So after the nine aligned answers I append two postscript messages built only from atoms already on the table: fist as zero, ✌ as yellow, 👌/🤞 as first/second wire. If Deaf saw real flashes, Deaf's own tally overrides me and the *scheme* still transfers for drilling the right rows next round.
